newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ProSieben TV sets IPO range 66-72 marks.
newsitem.headline: German ProSieben TV sets IPO range 66-72 marks.

text.p: German television group ProSieben Media AG said on Monday that the 17.5 million preference shares in its bourse listing would be offered to investors in a range of 66-72 marks a share.
Based on the share price range for the initial public offering, the first German television group to go public, the proceeds of the issue could be as high as 1.26 billion marks ($728.6 million).
The offering is one of Germany's most highly publicised since the huge offering last year of Deutsche Telekom AG .
Industry analysts have said that interest for European and particularly German media stocks is high because there are so few listed companies in the fast-changing sector.
"With the exception of Telekom, no other listing of a German company has generated as much public interest as the ProSieben share," said Georg Kofler, the company's chairman.
The final offer price will be announced on July 5 during the ProSieben nightly news broadcast at 1730 GMT and shares begin trading on July 7.
The IPO range, to be discussed with institutional investors during the subscription period that begins on June 24 and ends on July 3, was largely in line with market expectations of 62-80 marks.
Based on the IPO range, the offer would have a total volume of between 1.155 and 1.260 billion marks. The company's market capitalisation would be between 2.3 billion marks and 2.5 billion.
The company's equity ratio will probably be over 30 percent, it said in a statement.
The issue is being managed by a banking consortium that is led by BHF Bank AG, Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechselbank AG and Salomon Brothers.

Of the total number of non-voting preference shares, 15 million will be sold by Thomas Kirch, son of the Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, and another 2.5 million preferred shares will be created as part of a capital increase.

The capital increase will also create 2.5 million ordinary shares. As a result of the issue, Thomas Kirch will become ProSieben's largest shareholder with 60 percent of its voting ordinary shares. Retail group Rewe will hold the other 40 percent.

ProSieben will only benefit directly from the proceeds from the capital increase. It said it expects to add at least 330 million marks. The remaining proceeds from the sale of the preference shares to the market will go to Kirch.
